findings.finding: `Math.Round` has no decimals argument, so the bulk discount rounds to a whole number instead of 2 decimals. The plan says "rounded to 2 decimals as the coupons do". A 10-item order at 10.50 (subtotal 105.00) should get 5.25 but gets 5, so the customer is overcharged 0.25. A subtotal of 99.90 gives 4.995, which should be 5.00 and is 5 by luck. A subtotal of 30.00 gives 1.50, which rounds to 2 (banker's rounding) instead of 1.50, so the customer is undercharged 0.50. Any bulk order whose 5% has cents gets a wrong discount. The suite only uses round subtotals (10 items at 10.00), so it passes. Also raised by R1-S1 (spec).

The 5% never has cents, so wrong rounding passes. The current code rounds to whole units (a subtotal of 110.00 gives 5 instead of 5.50) and the suite is green (7 passed). Dropping the 2-digit argument, or using a different rounding mode, also passes.

findings.finding: No test has a coupon discount larger than the bulk discount with 10 or more items. The only coupon plus bulk test (`CouponAndBulk_LargerApplies`) has the bulk side winning (SAVE2 = 2.00 against 5.00). Code that always returned `bulk` when `ItemCount >= 10` would pass the whole suite. A WELCOME10 order with 10 items, where the 10% coupon should beat the 5% bulk, would fail it.

merged.finding: The plan's Design details say "5% of the subtotal, rounded to 2 decimals", and its Risks say to round "to 2 decimals as the coupons do". The code calls `Math.Round` with no digits argument, so it rounds to a whole unit. A subtotal of 110.00 gives 5 instead of 5.50. Criteria 1 and 2 still pass only because 10 items at 10.00 gives exactly 5.00. The criterion "5% bulk discount" is therefore built only in part: it is wrong for any subtotal whose 5% is not a whole number. The build record's Skipped section says "Only prices that make whole-cent discounts are tested", so no test catches this.
